NPCI INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE (Accepted)
-Yatharth Dedhia (CS)
OA ROUND (6/9/23):
SECTION A: Typical logical reasoning questions
●Few Graph analysis-related questions (time-consuming).
SECTION B: In-depth ML theory MCQ questions
●Topics related to random forests, probability, etc.
SECTION C: Essay writing on a given topic
SECTION D: 2 coding questions (easy-medium)
●Rat in a maze dp problem
●Dont remember the 2nd one (was easier)
Shortlist released (by 9/9/23)
After being shortlisted:
●Revised all the OS,DBMS,OOPs concepts and went through pyqs on
the internet.
●Revised all the imp basic algos (sorting, LL, DP, etc) which i had
already done previously in DSA 450 List
●Went through PPT to know more about the company and job role.
●Finalised intro.
●Went through all of my projects.
●Revised every tech stack used in projects.
●Went through ReactJS, SQL, OS, OOPs, DBMS interview questions
online.
●Took a mock interview with a friend to reduce nerves and improve
confidence and english speaking.
INTERVIEW (13/9/23):
●3 panelists (one of them was absent from mine)
●HR representative asked for my full name as per the aadhar card (twice
idk why).
●They asked if I was okay with joining at any of the centers (yes).

●They first asked me to introduce myself.
●What do you know about Python and C++
●What are classes
●What do you know about SQL
○I replied saying I haven't used it in any projects personally, as I
worked on the frontend part, but I am familiar with it as it was in
the coursework.
○I also briefly mentioned about the SQL query use and types (DDL,
DML, etc)
●He further asked what exactly is DDL, DML, etc and give example.
●Which ML algorithms do you know?
○I replied I am not well versed in ML algorithms, as I have worked
with DL only.
●Coding question: Count the number of words in a string
○Used C++
○Had to write the code, compile and run it with any example string
○Used counting the number of spaces and then adding 1 as the
logic, worked fine with them.
●How to find the middle element in a linked list (logic only, no code)
○First gave the naive approach which is to count the number of
nodes in LL and then go to the floor(n/2).
○He told me to optimize it.
○Explained the 2-pointer (fast and slow pointer) method.
○He was satisfied with it.
●HR round did not take place.
●Asked if I had any more questions.
○I asked, what tech stack we would get to work on during the
internship.
PERSONAL TIPS FOR INTERVIEWS:
Preparation:
●Never lie on your resume (about tech stacks too) as they can ask
anything from anything mentioned on your resume.
●Be thorough with your projects and tech stacks used in them and how
you used it, get some basic theoretical questions about it too. There are
plenty tech stack specific interview questions available online.

●Keep finalised, short (about 3-5mins) introduction ready as it is asked
in almost every interview. Get it corrected with any senior. (no need
to mug it up just remember the points).
●Intro should be about yourself, your skills, and what you learned from
your projects/experiences, rather than details about your
projects/experiences.
●Be prepared with STAR explanation for all of your projects beforehand.
●Go through the basic HR questions present online.
●Many interviewers ask about the hurdles (time/team management, etc)
in your project, be ready with it beforehand.
●Keep working copies of your project ready, they could ask for live
demos.
During the interviews:
●Be confident and calm, it is visible via your body language during the
interview.
●Take your time to think about the answer before you speak, you can
ask the interviewer for some time too (let me think about it).
●Don’t stray your answer away from the question.
●Clarify the question if you did not understand it.
●Be honest with your answers at all times.
●Explain any project or situation using STAR approach. Read examples
online if needed.
●In the end they might ask if you have any questions for them, ask at
least 1 question and genuinely be interested in it, and dont just ask for
the sake of asking.
Coding question in interviews:
●During any coding question clarify if they need just the algo explanation
or code as well.
●They might give you hints if you get stuck, try to pick-up on those hints
and try your best.
●Keep explaining through your thought process while explaining the algo.
●Start with the brute force solution, and build up upon that even if you
know the most optimal solution.
●Know the time/space complexity of the basic algos and what is the
reason for the same, complexity is almost always asked for any
question.

●Ask about the assumptions to be made for the questions (if they are
needed to be made).
●Ask for the constraints present for the question if any.
●It is fine if you dont get to the final solution, they are mostly interested in
your thought process and how you tackle the question and try to find the
solution.
